title: Interactions in Ecosystems
seo_title: Grade 7 Science: Interactions in Ecosystems Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe ecosystems in terms of biotic and abiotic factors; explain symbiotic relationships, energy flow and the cycling of matter; describe how populations are limited and how ecosystems change through succession. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand B: Life Systems – Interactions in the Environment)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 science worksheets on biotic and abiotic factors, symbiosis, energy pyramids, populations and succession. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Energy flows through food webs; matter cycles; populations are limited by resources.
body_html:
How to think about it

An ecosystem is the living (biotic) and non-living (abiotic) parts of an area and how they interact.

  • Symbiosis: mutualism (both benefit), commensalism (one benefits) and parasitism (one is harmed).
  • Only about 10% of the energy at one level passes to the next, so food chains are short.
  • Food, water, space and predators limit populations; succession slowly changes an ecosystem over time.
Example

A tick feeds on a moose. What relationship is this?

the tick benefits

the moose is harmed

Answer: parasitism

Example

Is sunlight biotic or abiotic?

it is not living

Answer: abiotic

Common mistakes

  • Thinking energy is recycled like matter (it flows one way).
  • Mixing up commensalism and mutualism.
  • Thinking populations can grow forever.

faq.q: What is the difference between biotic and abiotic factors?
faq.a: Biotic factors are living things. Abiotic factors are non-living, like sunlight, water and temperature.

faq.q: Why are there fewer top predators than producers?
faq.a: Energy is lost at each level, so there is less energy available for animals at the top.
The slow change in the plants and animals of an ecosystem over time, such as a burned forest growing back.

items.q: Ethan needs an example of predation (one organism hunts and eats another). Which is the best example?
c: squirrels and jays gather the same acorns
bees get nectar from flowers and carry pollen between them
oxpecker birds eat ticks off zebras
items.e: That is predation.

items.q: Nathan needs an example of parasitism (one benefits and the other is harmed). Which is the best example?
c: a lynx catches a snowshoe hare
fungi on plant roots get sugar and help roots take in water
bees get nectar from flowers and carry pollen between them
mistletoe takes water and nutrients from a tree
items.e: That is parasitism.

items.q: Ava observes that a lion hunts a zebra. What kind of interaction is this?

items.q: Emma observes that a frog eats a fly. What kind of interaction is this?

items.q: Fish in a pond die when the water becomes too acidic. Which physical factor is most important here?

items.q: Aiden observes that a mosquito feeds on a person's blood. What kind of interaction is this?

items.q: Few plants grow on the dark floor of a dense rainforest. Which physical factor is most important here?

items.q: Which is an abiotic factor?

items.q: What is symbiosis?
c: a close relationship between two different species

items.q: Pitcher plants catch insects because the soil is poor in nitrogen. Which physical factor is most important here?

items.q: What is succession?

the life cycle of a frog

items.q: Priya observes that barnacles ride on a whale without hurting it. What kind of interaction is this?

items.q: What is the role of producers in an ecosystem?
c: They capture the Sun's energy and make food by photosynthesis.
items.e: Producers are at the base.

items.q: Which organisms recycle nutrients from dead matter back into the soil?

items.q: After a forest fire in northern Ontario, what usually grows first?

items.q: Leah observes that fleas live on a cat. What kind of interaction is this?

items.q: Lichen is made of a fungus and an alga; the alga makes food and the fungus holds water. Which relationship is this?

items.q: Benjamin notes: “A dry summer leaves little water in a pond.” Which limiting factor is affecting the population?
items.e: A limiting factor is a resource that keeps a population from growing.

items.q: What is carrying capacity?
c: the weight an animal can carry
the largest population an ecosystem can support
the number of ecosystems on Earth
items.e: Food, water and space limit populations.

items.q: Olivia's graph shows the deer population in a forest over six years. What best explains why the population stopped growing?
c: The animals stopped having young forever.

items.e: Limited food, water and space keep the population from growing forever.
